overview.lead: Warriors tank or deal melee damage, and everything runs on Rage. Blizzard's deep dive singles out their sustained damage when several enemies are in melee range and the buffs and debuffs only Warriors bring. Their weak spot is recovering quickly from heavy damage.

points.text: Protection is Forever's shield tank, Fury is the dual-wield spec Warcraft Tavern points raiders to, and Arms suits a two-hander and is the guides' pick for battlegrounds.
Racials changed on 26 October: Human Ruthless is +1% crit and Dwarf Artisan's Precision is +1% hit with spells and attacks. No racial grants weapon skill.

101.summary: What every Warrior should know before choosing a spec: Rage, the class quests and the racial choice.

steps.text: Train Tactical Mastery at level 14: it keeps 10 Rage when you swap stances.
Use Victory Rush (level 20) within 20 seconds of a kill; it heals 10% of your maximum health.
Choose weapons for their damage and stats, not for Rage: Rage from your hits is normalized to weapon speed.
Count basic-attack crits as Rage income: they give bonus Rage.

mistakes.mistake: Picking a slow, hard-hitting weapon to generate more Rage.
mistakes.fix: Rage from your hits is normalized to weapon speed, so weapon damage no longer changes it.

mistakes.mistake: Treating Recklessness, Retaliation and Shield Wall as one shared cooldown.
mistakes.fix: They no longer share a cooldown, and Retaliation and Shield Wall are now 15-minute cooldowns.

steps.text: At level 10, take your race's Defensive Stance quest. Taunt and Sunder Armor are trained after it.
At level 20, look for your race's armor quest, which rewards the Fire Hardened Hauberk or the Brutal Hauberk.
At level 30, The Affray grants Berserker Stance and leads into the Whirlwind Weapon quest chain.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for Taunt at the trainer before the level 10 quest.
mistakes.fix: Defensive Stance comes from the quest, and Taunt and Sunder Armor are trained after it.

steps.text: A Dwarf Warrior gets +1% hit with spells and attacks from Artisan's Precision.
A Human Warrior gets +1% crit from Ruthless, cut from 2% on 26 October.
Leave weapon skill out of the choice: no racial grants it in Forever.

mistakes.mistake: Using an older guide that gives Ruthless 2% crit.
mistakes.fix: Ruthless is +1% crit since the 26 October notes.

mistakes.mistake: Choosing a race for a weapon-skill bonus.
mistakes.fix: No racial grants weapon skill in Forever.

overview.lead: Arms suits a two-handed weapon: Two-Handed Weapon Specialization sits in the tree, Mortal Strike is at the bottom, and Bloodthrill gives you Overpower chances while your Rend is on the target.

points.text: Weaponmaster replaces the old per-weapon specializations, so any weapon you pick up gets a bonus: crit for axes and polearms, armor ignore for maces and staves, extra attacks for swords.
Warcraft Tavern presents Arms mainly as a battleground spec that still works in raids, with Fury as its raid pick.

101.summary: Leveling as Arms, the core rotation and the Rage habits that matter first.

steps.text: Warcraft Tavern's author calls Arms the traditional leveling pick and prefers Bloodthrill over Weaponmaster while leveling.
Victory Rush (level 20) stays usable for 20 seconds after a kill and heals 10% of your maximum health, so open the next pull with it.
Sweeping Strikes makes your next 5 melee attacks hit an extra nearby enemy, which helps when two mobs are on you.
Tactical Mastery keeps 10 Rage when you swap stances. Improved Tactical Mastery retains another 5, 10 or 15 Rage for one, two or three points.

mistakes.mistake: Saving points for Mortal Strike without taking Sweeping Strikes.
mistakes.fix: Mortal Strike requires Sweeping Strikes, so take Sweeping Strikes on the way down.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for Axe, Mace, Sword or Polearm Specialization.
mistakes.fix: Arms combines the old weapon specializations into Weaponmaster.

steps.text: Open with Charge for Rage, then put Rend on the target so your main-hand swings can enable Overpower.
Use Mortal Strike on cooldown and Overpower whenever it lights up.
Fit Slam in while Mortal Strike cools down. Its base cooldown is 15 seconds, and Improved Slam keeps it from delaying your swing.
Spend spare Rage on Heroic Strike, or on Cleave when two or more enemies stand close.
Finish low-health targets with Execute.

mistakes.mistake: Letting Rend fall off the target.
mistakes.fix: Bloodthrill only gives Overpower chances against your Rend target, so keep Rend up.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing Slam ahead of Mortal Strike.
mistakes.fix: Use Mortal Strike on cooldown and fit Slam into the gaps while it cools down.

steps.text: Rage from your own hits depends on weapon speed, not weapon damage, so a stronger weapon of the same speed adds damage but no extra Rage.
Crits from basic attacks give extra Rage (a 100% bonus since 1 October), so crit feeds both damage and Rage.
Spearing Strike needs Battle Stance, costs 15 Rage and has a 20 sec cooldown. It deals extra damage to Giants, Dragonkin and mounted targets, and dismounts riders.
The Legacy perk Talented can start your talent points earlier; guides disagree on how much.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting a bigger weapon of the same speed to give more Rage.
mistakes.fix: Rage from your hits is normalized to weapon speed, so it does not.

201.summary: Level-60 builds, stat priorities, consumables, the raid and PvP.

steps.text: Open a build in the talent calculator and check it against your talents in game before you spend points.
Weaponmaster at 5/5 gives +5% crit with axes and polearms, ignores 15% of armor with maces and staves, or gives a 5% chance of an extra attack with swords.
Two-Handed Weapon Specialization raises two-handed weapon damage by 6% at rank 3 of 3.

mistakes.mistake: Counting on Shield Bash or Shield Slam to trigger Weaponmaster's sword effect.
mistakes.fix: They no longer trigger it.

steps.text: Get hit from gear or the Dwarf racial: Furious Precision is the only Warrior talent that adds hit, and it covers off-hand attacks only.
Treat the hit cap as unknown until Blizzard or reviewed logs give a number.
Count +1% hit for a Dwarf and +1% crit for a Human.

mistakes.mistake: Taking Furious Precision for main-hand hit.
mistakes.fix: It increases your chance to hit with off-hand attacks only.

steps.text: Plan raid nights without world buffs: Icy Veins says they are removed inside raids.
Bring Elixir of the Grizzly: +25 Strength and +2% crit for 30 minutes.
Buy healing potions from a First Aid crafter: they are no longer an Alchemy craft.
Eat Smoked Desert Dumplings (+20 Strength) or Grilled Squid (+1% crit). Both need an Iron Oven camp object (Cooking 300).

mistakes.mistake: Planning to drink two flasks.
mistakes.fix: In the Classic reference only one flask is active at a time, and it persists through death.

mistakes.mistake: Counting on world buffs inside the raid.
mistakes.fix: Icy Veins' raid overview says world buffs are removed inside raids.

steps.text: Expect Fury to be the raid pick: Warcraft Tavern presents Arms as a battleground spec that is still viable in PvE.
Recklessness gives +100% crit chance for 15 seconds while you take 20% more damage, and it no longer shares a cooldown with Retaliation or Shield Wall.
Keep Sunder Armor going alongside a Rogue's Expose Armor.

mistakes.mistake: Holding Recklessness back because Shield Wall was used.
mistakes.fix: Recklessness no longer shares a cooldown with Retaliation or Shield Wall.

steps.text: Arms is the usual PvP Warrior spec: Mortal Strike cuts healing on the target by 50% for 10 seconds, Improved Hamstring can root, and Spearing Strike knocks riders off their mounts.
Improved Berserker Rage can remove movement-impairing effects, Iron Will shortens stuns and fears, and Victory Rush heals you after kills.
Piercing Howl (Fury row 3) dazes every enemy within 10 yards, slowing them by 50% for 6 seconds.

Against Hunters: Wyvern Sting is gone, Scorpid Sting now lowers your hit chance by 2%, and all traps share one 30-second cooldown and can be laid in combat. Auto Shot needs a brief stand-still, so keep the pressure on.
Against Rogues: Sap no longer breaks a Rogue's Stealth, and Distract now warns you that a Rogue is near. Improved Berserker Rage can clear movement-impairing effects.

mistakes.mistake: Saving Mortal Strike for damage only.
mistakes.fix: It also reduces the effectiveness of any healing on the target by 50% for 10 sec, so use it while the target is being healed.

overview.lead: Fury dual-wields one-handed weapons for steady damage. Warcraft Tavern names it the main PvE Warrior spec, with strong cleave from Cleave and Whirlwind.

points.text: Bloodthirst no longer heals: it hits for 45% of your Attack Power plus 30 and gives you 10% movement speed for 10 seconds.
Death Wish leads to Bloodthirst. Flurry no longer needs Death Wish, and Death Wish increases the damage you take while it is active.

101.summary: Leveling as Fury, the core rotation and dual-wield basics.

steps.text: Warcraft Tavern rates every Warrior spec viable for leveling but says Fury takes more damage and has more downtime.
Blood Craze heals you a little after you take a critical strike or a big hit, and Gore Drinker heals on your next swings after Enrage, Bloodrage, Berserker Rage, Death Wish or Bloodthirst.
Enrage can trigger from any damaging attack you take, so its damage bonus is up often while you level.

mistakes.mistake: Taking Death Wish because Flurry needs it.
mistakes.fix: Flurry no longer needs Death Wish; Death Wish leads to Bloodthirst.

steps.text: Keep Battle Shout up; it now buffs the whole raid.
Use Bloodthirst on cooldown, then Whirlwind. Improved Whirlwind cuts Whirlwind's cooldown by 2 sec at rank 2 of 2.
Spend extra Rage on Heroic Strike against one target, or Cleave against several.
Use Death Wish with your other cooldowns: 20% more Physical damage for 30 seconds, at the cost of taking more damage.
Switch to Execute when the target is low; Improved Execute lowers its Rage cost.

mistakes.mistake: Using Death Wish while the raid takes heavy damage.
mistakes.fix: Death Wish raises all damage you take, so time it away from heavy raid damage.

steps.text: Dual-wield auto attacks miss more often than special attacks. Furious Precision is the only Warrior talent that adds hit, and it covers off-hand attacks only.
Queuing Heroic Strike no longer raises your off-hand hit chance in Forever.
Unbridled Wrath no longer doubles its Rage with two-handed weapons.
Lingering Rage delays Rage decay after combat, so you carry Rage into the next pull.

mistakes.mistake: Queuing Heroic Strike to raise off-hand hit.
mistakes.fix: That no longer works; off-hand hit comes from Furious Precision.

overview.lead: Protection is Forever's shield tank: Defiance's threat bonus and Bastion's damage bonus only work while a shield is equipped.

points.text: Blocks, dodges and parries feed Rage through Shield Specialization and Master of Defense, and Vanguard lets you Charge in Defensive Stance.
Shield Slam causes very high threat, grows with your block value and has a 50% chance to dispel a magic effect on the target.

101.summary: Leveling as Protection, tanking your first dungeons and the Rage rules for tanks.

steps.text: Warcraft Tavern rates all three Warrior specs viable for leveling, but its Protection guide says the spec does poorly when you are not tanking.
Defensive Stance comes from the level 10 class quest, and Taunt and Sunder Armor are trained after it.
Rend and Sunder Armor tag mobs instantly, so you claim shared quest mobs quickly.

mistakes.mistake: Tanking without a shield.
mistakes.fix: Defiance and Bastion keep their shield requirement, so equip one.

steps.text: Charge in (Vanguard keeps you in Defensive Stance), then Shield Slam.
On packs, use Thunder Clap and Demoralizing Shout. Thunder Clap scales with Attack Power and works in Defensive Stance, and Demoralizing Shout threatens every target it hits.
Use Revenge whenever it is available, and Sunder Armor to build threat on your main target; Sunder threat scales with Attack Power.
Spend spare Rage on Heroic Strike once your threat is solid.
Save Last Stand and Shield Wall for emergencies; Improved Shield Wall shortens Shield Wall's cooldown.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing Shield Slam without a shield equipped.
mistakes.fix: Shield Slam requires a shield, and its damage grows with your Block Value.

steps.text: Rage from damage taken now ignores your armor and absorbs, so a Power Word: Shield on you no longer costs you Rage.
Last Stand gives you 30% of your maximum health for 20 sec and has a 3 min cooldown.
Thunder Clap's threat was lowered to balance its new damage, so pair it with Demoralizing Shout on big pulls.
Shield Slam needs a shield, so use it whenever it is ready.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting to keep Last Stand's extra health.
mistakes.fix: After the effect expires, the health is lost.

Improved Disarm shortens Disarm's cooldown, and Iron Will shortens stuns and fears on you.
